newsitem.title: USA: Ill. tollway trustee seeks to intervene in lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: Ill. tollway trustee seeks to intervene in lawsuit.

text.p: An attorney representing First Chicago NBD Corp's First National Bank of Chicago unit, the bond trustee for $940 million of Illinois State Toll Highway Authority bonds, asked a state judge Wednesday to allow the bank to intervene in a taxpayer challenge to the authority's budget practices.

Attorney Terry Moritz said the bank acted as quickly as was appropriate to protect the interests of bondholders. Cook County Judge Stephen Schiller did not rule on the issue, but set a briefing schedule to consider the bank's motion.

Schiller entered a formal order Wednesday granting a preliminary injunction to the taxpayers challenging the Toll Authority's appropriations and staying it until December 15 to give the General Assembly an opportunity to approve a budget.
The Toll Authority will appeal Schiller's finding in the meantime, Chief Legal Counsel George Sotos said.

Schiller ruled in late May that the Toll Authority budget practices of making ongoing appropriation without oversight of the governor or lawmakers falls short of Illinois' constitutional requirements.

Moritz had sought to intervene in the lawsuit before entry of a preliminary injunction contending that Schiller did not fully understand how an order enjoining the Toll Authority expenditures would impact bondholders.

The terms under which the bonds were sold make specific spending requirements on the Toll Authority which must be met and the order to be entered Wednesday does not completely protect bondholders, Moritz said.
Sotos did not oppose the bond trustee's intervention, but asked the court to proceed with the preliminary injunction action to accelerate the appeals process.

Attorney Lee Schwartz representing taxpayers challenging the authority's budjet practices objected to the intervention, contending that First Chicago had had several months to seek intervention in the lawsuit, which was disclosed in legal documents for a bond issuance by the Toll Authority last fall.

In the end, Schiller entered the preliminary injunction order and gave all parties seven court days to respond to the First Chicago request. The parties are scheduled to return to court on June 24 for a status hearing on the trustee's motion.

Moody's Investor's Service on Tuesday said Schiller's ruling could change the fundamental nature of the Toll Authority's credit by requiring third party oversight of the agency's operations if it is upheld on an expected appeal to the Illinois Supreme Court .
Failure to maintain protections for current bondholders would result in a rating revision, Moody's said.

"This would jeopardize the agency's fiscal autonomy and could and pose significant credit concerns," Moody's said in a statement. "This appears to be the first instance in the United States where a state government would have direct budgetary control of an independent toll agency."
